Singer, Adekunle Gold, through his foundation, has partnered with global financial platform, Pesa, to kick off a $20,000 initiative aimed at supporting organisations working to improve the lives of people living with sickle cell disease. The programme, tagged “We’re Not Done: AG Foundation Sickle Cell Impact Initiative”, will provide funding to selected organisations to strengthen their work in healthcare access, patient support, education, awareness and advocacy. According to a statement announcing the initiative, the inaugural funding will support four organisations alongside the Adekunle Gold Foundation: Sickle Cell Advocacy Management Initiative in Nigeria, Not Just You in Canada, Sickle Life in Ghana and It Takes A Village in the United Kingdom. The funding is expected to help the beneficiaries strengthen existing programmes, expand their reach and improve support for people living with the condition. Gold, who has spoken publicly about living with sickle cell disease, said the initiative was designed to translate awareness into practical support for affected individuals and families. There are incredible organisations working every day to improve the lives of people living with sickle cell, and together with Pesa, we want to give them more resources to do that work and reach even more people.” From compliance to partnership — Becoming an advocate for your own Sickle Cell care Advocacy vs compliance: Finding your voice in sickle cell care Learning to nourish a body under pressure Pesa is partnering with the foundation to support the launch and first cycle of the programme. The company’s Head of Global Growth and Marketing, Tosin Olaniyi, said sickle cell disease affected many people within the Nigerian and wider Black communities served by the platform. “These are our friends, colleagues, and loved ones. Adekunle Gold has shown how a personal connection to an issue can become a force for meaningful change, and we’re proud to support the launch of We’re Not Done, an initiative dedicated to raising awareness and supporting the sickle cell community,” Olaniyi said. He added that the partnership aimed to move beyond awareness campaigns by providing tangible support to individuals and families affected by the condition. Through the initiative, the foundation and Pesa hope to combine funding, advocacy and public visibility to strengthen organisations working within the sickle cell community and promote lasting impact.
